Job Description

30% - Fire and Life Safety Compliance Program Management

Charleston Division Fire Marshal and Program Oversight

Serves as the designated Charleston Division Fire Marshal and provides technical authority for fire and life safety compliance activities throughout Charleston Division facilities.
Directs and administers the Charleston Division Fire and Life Safety Program and establishes program goals, priorities, policies, standards, and performance measures.
Provides leadership and strategic direction for organizational fire prevention, life safety, code compliance, and regulatory readiness activities.
Serves as the primary liaison with Facilities Management, Construction Management, Public Safety, Emergency Management, Clinical Operations, Research Leadership, and Executive Leadership on fire and life safety matters.

Inspection and Corrective Action Program Management

Oversees fire and life safety inspection programs conducted by staff, contractors, and regulatory agencies.
Ensures identified deficiencies are documented, prioritized, assigned, and resolved through established corrective action processes.
Reviews inspection data, identifies trends, and develops corrective action strategies to reduce organizational risk.
Provides guidance and oversight regarding fire and life safety repairs, barrier management, fire door compliance, and corrective maintenance activities.

Fire Protection Systems and Equipment Oversight

Oversees inspection, testing, maintenance, and compliance activities associated with fire alarm systems, fire sprinkler systems, fire suppression systems, standpipe systems, fire extinguishers, and passive fire protection systems.
Ensures required monthly, annual, and periodic inspections are completed by qualified personnel and vendors.
Evaluates program performance and regulatory compliance associated with fire protection systems.

Emergency Preparedness and Fire Drill Program Administration

Directs and oversees organizational fire drill and evacuation exercise programs.
Ensures fire drills are conducted, documented, evaluated, and reviewed in accordance with regulatory and accreditation requirements.
Oversees development and maintenance of facility-specific fire response plans, evacuation procedures, and emergency management support documents.

Fire and Life Safety Incident Management

Leads or coordinates reviews of fire and life safety incidents and events.
Evaluates incident trends and recommends corrective actions, policy revisions, and program improvements.
Coordinates reporting requirements with internal stakeholders and external agencies as appropriate.

30% - Fire and Life Safety Operations, Regulatory Compliance and Reporting

Vendor and Contract Management

Develops, administers, and monitors contracts related to fire alarm systems, fire suppression systems, fire doors, fire extinguishers, passive fire protection systems, and related services.
Evaluates vendor performance and ensures contracted services meet applicable regulatory, accreditation, and organizational requirements.
Assists with budget planning, forecasting, and resource allocation for fire and life safety programs.

Program Data Management and Reporting

Establishes and maintains fire and life safety performance metrics and compliance dashboards.
Collects, analyzes, and interprets program data to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.
Prepares reports and presentations for executive leadership, Environment of Care Committees, Safety Committees, and other governing bodies.
Maintains records associated with inspection, testing, maintenance, and compliance activities for regulatory review.

Code Interpretation and Technical Consultation

Serves as the organization's subject matter expert on NFPA codes and standards, International Fire Code, International Building Code, Joint Commission standards, and other applicable fire and life safety regulations.
Provides technical consultation to Facilities Management, Construction Management, Clinical Operations, Research Programs, Public Safety, and administrative departments.
Reviews operational and facility changes to ensure compliance with fire and life safety requirements.

Regulatory Oversight and Agency Coordination

Serves as the primary organizational point of contact during inspections, surveys, audits, and regulatory reviews involving fire and life safety compliance.
Coordinates readiness activities for Joint Commission, CMS, State Fire Marshal, local fire department, and other regulatory inspections.
Ensures deficiencies identified during surveys or inspections are properly documented, assigned, tracked, and resolved.

Construction and Renovation Compliance

Reviews construction, renovation, occupancy, and space-use change projects for compliance with fire and life safety requirements.
Collaborates with project teams during planning, design, construction, and occupancy phases.
Provides recommendations regarding life safety impacts, fire protection requirements, and regulatory expectations.

20% - Environment of Care and Life Safety Program Administration

Fire and Life Safety Management Plan Administration

Serves as administrator of the Charleston Division Fire and Life Safety Management Plan.
Develops, implements, and evaluates strategies to ensure compliance with Joint Commission, CMS, state, and local requirements.
Conducts annual program evaluations and performance assessments and recommends improvements to leadership.

Environment of Care Leadership

Serves as a key advisor to Environment of Care, Safety, Emergency Management, and Executive Leadership Committees.
Presents fire and life safety performance metrics, compliance findings, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations.
Coordinates fire and life safety initiatives across healthcare, academic, research, and administrative environments.

Building Rounds and Deficiency Management

Oversees fire and life safety components of Environment of Care rounds and organizational compliance assessments.
Ensures deficiencies are documented, prioritized, assigned, and reconciled in a timely manner.
Monitors compliance trends and develops initiatives to improve organizational performance.

15% - Leadership and Staff Development

Fire and Life Safety Team Leadership

Provides direct supervision, leadership, mentoring, and professional development for Fire and Life Safety personnel.
Establishes operational priorities, staffing plans, performance expectations, and workload management processes.
Conducts performance evaluations and supports employee development and succession planning activities.
Ensures staff maintain required certifications, competencies, and regulatory knowledge.
Fosters a culture of accountability, customer service, collaboration, continuous improvement, and regulatory excellence.

Performs other related duties and responsibilities as assigned to support organizational goals and operational needs.

Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technology has an exciting opportunity for a Program Manager
located in Kettering, OH (Dayton, WPAFB) to support our EPASS GB contract. As part of the AFLCMC/GB Business and Enterprise Systems Directorate, the Reliability and Maintainability Information System (REMIS) is the primary Air Force (AF) enterprise maintenance data system used for collecting, validating, editing, standardizing, and reporting equipment maintenance information on a global world-wide basis. REMIS consists of a fully integrated relational database providing a single source of all reportable AF weapon system data to over 1,100 authorized AF users. REMIS is a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) financial feeder system that provides accounting/accountability of all AF aerospace vehicles (F-35, F22, F-15, F-16, A- 10, C-130, C-17, C-5, etc.), Mine Resistant Ambush Protected (MRAP) vehicles and ICBMs. It provides real time status on aircraft and weapon systems combat readiness, availability, reliability, maintainability, trend analysis, failure prediction, utilization,

and configuration status. The REMIS supplement RDT&E efforts are focused on modernizing and improving this Air Force capability.

Role

The Program Manager
will have comprehensive knowledge of principles, policies and practices of systems acquisition and program management, as defined in DoWI 5000.02 and 5000.75, as well as knowledge of roles and relationships within the DoW and the Air Force. Program management resources shall have:

Knowledge of qualitative and quantitative techniques for gathering, analyzing, and measuring the effectiveness, efficiency and productivity of acquisition programs;
Knowledge of support activities that assist the program manager in assessing what programs are within schedule and cost baselines and be able to recommend viable solutions to problems as well as the pursuit of alternative courses of action;
Abilities to effectively communicate orally and in writing, providing quality acquisition and program documentation, e.g., briefings, documents, and plans;
Abilities to plan, research, analyze and assess system acquisition in terms of development, production and deployment of weapons systems and associated equipment;
Abilities to formulate plans and recommend effective strategies in meeting cost, schedule and performance objectives;
Abilities to support and develop acquisition reports, including statutory and regulatory reports, e.g., Defense Acquisition Executive Summary (DAES) or Monthly Activity Report (MAR);
Abilities to support program management reviews, senior level meeting/reviews and Integrated Master Plan (IMP)/Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) reviews; and,
Abilities to support and develop various briefings/schedules of program status and acquisition tasks to senior management.

The Program Manager Possesses the advanced knowledge, experience and recognized ability to be considered highly skilled in their technical/professional field. Possesses the ability to perform tasks independently and oversee the efforts of junior and journeyman contractor personnel within the technical/professional discipline. Demonstrates advanced knowledge of their technical/professional discipline as well as possess a comprehensive understanding and ability to apply associated standards, procedures, and practices in their area of expertise (Program Office, Enterprise and Staff Level Support interface).

U.S. Citizenship.
Advanced Degree (MA/MS) in Business Administration, Management Information Systems or other relevant discipline and 10 years of experience, 5 of which must be in the DoW, or
BA/BS Degree in Business Administration, Management Information Systems or other relevant discipline and 12 years of experience in the respective technical/professional discipline being performed, 5 of which must be in the DoW, or,
15 years of directly related experience with proper certifications, 8 of which must be in the DoW.
Candidate must possess and maintain a T1/NACI clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

Must be familiar with using MS Teams and MS SharePoint for project collaboration.
Experience with managing Air Force Risk Management process in support of the acquisition process.

PMI Certified Program Management Professional (PMP)
Agile Certifications

Job Description

Senior Project Manager, IT Infrastructure Readiness, Epic Connect THP/HH

Associate Vice-President, Epic Connect THP/HH

THP Chief Technology and Security Officer and HH IT and security leadership

Posted:
Tuesday, October 20, 2026 – Tuesday, November 3, 2026

Strategic Context

Trillium Health Partners (THP) and Halton Healthcare (HH) are formally exploring whether HH should join THP’s Epic environment through Epic Connect. The due diligence and planning phase is focused on the assessment and planning to validate the opportunity, confirm requirements, and determine the recommended direction. It does not represent a final implementation decision or commitment.

Together, HH and THP aim to create a more connected, accessible and digitally enabled regional system of care that improves patient outcomes, strengthens team and learner experience, and makes the best use of public resources for the communities they serve.

The potential partnership is a clinical transformation enabled by digital, operational, and governance alignment. The due diligence and planning phase will assess clinical workflow and THP foundation fit, technical and infrastructure requirements, scope, total cost of ownership, resourcing, governance, organizational readiness, stakeholder engagement and the future operating model. Findings will inform a proposed Epic Collaboration Agreement and implementation recommendation for approval by the appropriate governance bodies.

The Position

The Senior Project Manager, IT Infrastructure Readiness will lead the technical, infrastructure and application readiness stream for the due diligence and planning phase, while helping design a scalable technical and service foundation for future shared digital offerings. The role will coordinate the evidence required to determine whether the capacity, security, integration, identity, device, data and support foundations can safely and sustainably enable a shared Epic environment.

If the organizations proceed following due diligence, the role will transition into the implementation team, supporting detailed planning, clinical workflow alignment, organizational readiness, implementation execution, go-live, and post-go-live stabilization while maintaining continuity of decisions, risks and interdependencies. This role will help ensure a seamless transition from planning into implementation and adoption across THP and Halton Healthcare.

Key Accountabilities

Lead technical scope validation across infrastructure, networks, hosting, cloud/data center, end-user computing, clinical and non-clinical devices, identity and access, integration, third-party applications, data, monitoring, backup, disaster recovery and service management.
Coordinate a THP hardware and security capacity assessment, provide HH IT and security personnel a reasonable opportunity to review it, and benchmark security against an appropriate recognized standard or framework used in the Ontario public-hospital sector.
Identify additional hardware, software, licensing, supplier, connectivity, integration, staffing and operating resources required to validate scope and inform the proposed Epic Collaboration Agreement.
Protect the stability, security and performance of THP’s Epic environment and incorporate continuity-of-care and downtime requirements into technical recommendations.
Address personal and personal health information safeguards, access, data custodianship, HH access to extraction of data, and data-transition assistance requirements for the future model.
Coordinate Epic, supplier and third-party technical dependencies, approvals, deliverables, performance oversight and change control.
Develop technical risk, issue, dependency, assumption and decision records and escalate material items into the program and Joint Steering Committee for governance.
Validate technical capital and operating implications for TCO, cost recovery, procurement, implementation, and lifecycle planning.
Define future-state technical support, maintenance, service levels, monitoring, incident/problem/change management, capacity planning, partner communication and escalation.
Prepare executive recommendations that explain technical options, risks, costs, trade-offs, and implications in patient-care and business terms.

What Success Looks Like

Both organizations have an evidence-based understanding of technical scope, capacity, security, gaps, and investment requirements.
A reviewed hardware and security capacity assessment supports the partnership recommendation.
Technical risks to patient care, privacy, cybersecurity, resilience, and THP platform performance are explicit and owned.
The future technical support, maintenance, data and service model is defined for the proposed agreement and designed to scale for additional partners and services where approved.
Technical costs, resources, suppliers, and implementation dependencies are integrated into TCO and the future plan.

Qualifications and Leadership Profile

Undergraduate degree in information technology, computer science, engineering, cybersecurity, business or related field required; graduate education is an asset.
At least 5 years of progressive technology project or program leadership in a complex, highly available and regulated environment.
Experience leading infrastructure and technical readiness for enterprise platforms, HIS/EHR transformation, multi-site integration, or shared services.
Knowledge of architecture, cybersecurity, identity, networks, devices, integration, data, resilience, service management, TCO and vendor oversight; health care and Epic experience are strongly preferred.
Strategic technology integrator who can connect architecture to service strategy, scalability and system outcomes, while maintaining disciplined risk, resilience and delivery focus.

Important Posting Notes

This is a two-year role. Final employment status, salary band, work location, screening requirements, and posting dates will be confirmed by THP Human Resources. The role requires work across THP and HH sites and disciplined handling of confidential, personal and personal-health information.

The Port of San Francisco is an enterprise agency of the City and County of San Francisco and is governed by a Commission of five members appointed by the Mayor. The Port Commission is responsible for overseeing a broad range of waterfront commercial, maritime, and public access facilities that are held in public trust for the people of California. The Port’s jurisdiction covers approximately 7.5 miles of waterfront land from Pier 98, near Hunter’s Point in the southern part of San Francisco, to Fisherman’s Wharf in the northern part of the City.

The Port’s diverse business portfolio includes over 550 ground, commercial, retail, office, industrial and maritime industrial leases including cargo shipping, layberthing, excursion boats, ferry boats, fishing and fish processing/distribution, tourism, filming, harbor services, and cruise operations. With some of the most flexible cargo handling facilities on the West Coast, as well as naturally deep water, the Port can handle various types of cargo such as, dry-bulk, neo-bulk, roll-on/roll-off, and project cargoes.

The Port of San Francisco has many internationally recognized landmarks such as Fisherman’s Wharf, Pier 39, the Exploratorium, the Ferry Building and Oracle Park, home of the San Francisco Giants baseball team. With its unique and historic properties, the Port is home to a variety of tenants and uses. The Port Commission over the last five decades has led a remarkable transformation of the Port; maintaining its industrial maritime heritage while developing new uses, including commercial and public activities, that have helped San Francisco remain one of the most visited and popular cities on the globe.

For more information about the Port of San Francisco, visit SFPort.com. Follow us on Twitter and Facebook.

The Port’s Technology Team

The Port Technology Team manages the Port’s enterprise applications, its network and technology infrastructure and provides support to the Port’s staff. The Port is embarking on a foundational modernization program, led by the technology team, that will transform the systems the Port uses to execute its businesses and operations and improve efficiency and visibility for staff and leadership.

Job Description

The Senior IT Project Manager will lead project and product management activities for the Port Modernization Project, a comprehensive initiative consisting of multiple interrelated technology projects designed to modernize the Port's business systems and operations. Key initiatives include the development and implementation of an enterprise-scale Salesforce-based system, configuration and implementation of Kahua, a construction project management platform, modernization of harbor management systems, integration with the City's PermitSF and People & Pay systems, and development of a comprehensive payments infrastructure. The position will also support additional technology modernization initiatives as the program evolves.

The essential duties of this position include, but are not limited to, the following:

Develop project roadmaps, timelines, and implementation strategies to support the Port Modernization Project.
Establish and manage project schedules, milestones, deliverables, and priorities to ensure timely execution.
Collaborate with technical leads and key stakeholders to establish product direction, evaluate feature tradeoffs, and prioritize project requirements.
Organize and coordinate advisory groups and stakeholder committees to facilitate project planning, decision-making, and implementation.
Partner with user researchers and external consultants to plan and guide user research, discovery, and requirements-gathering activities.
Identify and assess user needs in collaboration with technical teams and Port stakeholders to ensure technology solutions align with business and operational requirements.
Evaluate and improve business workflows and processes in collaboration with user researchers and Port staff to enhance operational efficiency.
Prepare and present project status reports, progress updates, and recommendations to internal and external stakeholders, including Port leadership.
Identify and engage change champions across Port business units to support organizational readiness, user adoption, and feedback on new technology solutions.
Manage and prioritize project and product backlogs to align development activities with business needs and project objectives.
Lead and facilitate Agile ceremonies, including sprint planning, backlog refinement, sprint demonstrations, and retrospectives.
Build consensus among stakeholders to resolve competing priorities, address project challenges, and support informed decision-making.
Serve as the Port's product owner for technology solutions implemented by external partners, providing direction and ensuring deliverables meet business requirements.

A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or other related field; AND four (4) years of experience implementing and managing integrated information systems projects; OR
Eight (8) years of experience implementing and managing integrated information systems projects.

jobs.title: Technical Infrastructure Program Manager, Global Connectivity Infrastructure Development - Fiber Deployment
jobs.description:
Description

Application deadline: Oct 22, 2026

Bringing a new AWS data center online starts with fiber in the ground. In this role you own that work across high-volume US metro markets, taking a metro fiber route from approved plan to live capacity and managing the construction vendors who build it.

You will run several builds at once, hold vendors to schedule and quality, inspect sites to confirm the work was done right, and keep a wide group of stakeholders current on where each project stands. If you have built fiber before, you will move fast here. If you have run complex physical infrastructure or construction programs in another field, you can succeed here too: the hard part of this job is owning an ambiguous program end to end and driving it to delivery, and we will teach you the fiber.

Key job responsibilities

Own end-to-end delivery of metro fiber construction projects, from approved plan through in-service handover
Manage construction vendors to schedule and quality: track milestones, measure performance, and drive corrective action when standards are not met
Run quality control across the build: inspect conduit and vault installation, validate designs in the field, and review splice and fiber acceptance test results and as-built accuracy before handoff to internal customers
Deliver weekly status reporting to leadership and internal customers, and manage risk, escalations, and competing priorities across multiple concurrent builds
Coordinate site access and approvals in security-regulated environments, and travel to field sites up to 50% of the time

A day in the life

Most days your focus is knowing the true status of every build you own and moving each one forward. You will scan vendor progress and open risks, make the calls that unblock a permit or a crew, and update the trackers your stakeholders rely on. You work day to day with construction vendors and general contractors, fiber engineers, data center and networking teams, and permitting authorities. Some weeks you will be on a site confirming the build matches the design and the test results hold up. Beyond the steady work of delivery, you will also help improve the standards and processes the team runs on. This is a field-facing role rather than a remote one, and you will spend real time on site.

About The Team

Global Connectivity Infrastructure Development - Fiber Deployment plans, manages, and delivers the physical fiber network that connects AWS data centers. The high-volume metro team delivers the fiber that brings new AWS capacity online across our busiest metro markets. You will work alongside construction vendors, engineers, and the internal customers who depend on that capacity, building large-scale fiber networks on time and to a high quality bar. Our focus for the coming years is scaling delivery without losing that quality, and this role is central to it. New teammates reach independent project ownership quickly, supported by runbooks and mentorship.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of technical infrastructure management experience
Knowledge of best practices and emerging technologies, related to infrastructure (i.e. network, data center, hardware, software)
Experience with varying scenarios of infrastructure builds
Bachelor's degree in engineering, project management, construction management or similar technical focus
3+ years of experience managing third-party vendors or contractors, including tracking delivery timelines, measuring performance against metrics, and driving corrective action when quality or schedule standards are not met
3+ years of experience managing multiple concurrent projects across cross-functional teams, including scope, schedule, risk, and stakeholder communication

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a network planning, network construction/implementation, or commercial implementation role at an ISP, telecoms operator, or Hyperscaler
2+ years of fiber handling and fiber installation processes experience, or experience with cabling infrastructure best practices and methodologies
Experience reading and interpreting construction drawings and specifications
Experience with large scale infrastructure
PMP certificate
Experience with reporting and automation tools such as SQL, Python, GIS platforms, or business intelligence tools
Experience delivering physical infrastructure in another domain such as data center, utilities, energy, or large-scale capital construction, and applying it to a new technical field

jobs.description:
About The Team

Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) builds compliance programs and provides assurance for OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We combine technical understanding with practical operations to reduce risk, support product and research teams, and produce reliable evidence of how our controls work.

About The Role

As a Regulatory Compliance Program Manager, you will build and operate programs that turn regulatory requirements into clear responsibilities, effective processes, and evidence that can withstand external scrutiny.

Your work will focus on AI safety/security and content moderation, with privacy operations as an adjacent area. You will partner with Legal and the teams that build and operate our products to scope the work, maintain accurate control narratives, prepare regulatory responses, and lead external assessments for your assigned portfolio.

You should be comfortable owning delivery, explaining tradeoffs, and changing your recommendation when the evidence changes. Success means controls have accountable owners, evidence stays current, and teams can respond accurately without repeatedly rebuilding the same work. The initial portfolio and expectations will be agreed with the hiring manager.

In This Role, You Will

Lead an agreed portfolio of AI safety/security and content-compliance work, including programs associated with the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, with Legal and relevant experts confirming applicable requirements.
Translate requirements into scoped programs, operating processes, control and evidence responsibilities, milestones, and clear escalation paths.
Build and maintain accurate control narratives and traceable evidence for regulatory requests, reporting, audits, and assessments.
Lead preparation and delivery for external compliance assessments, coordinate the responsible teams, and track gaps through verified resolution or an explicitly owned decision.
Prioritize the work that materially improves compliance outcomes and reduces risk; explain what should proceed, change, or wait and why.
Develop evidence-backed recommendations with Legal, Product, Security, Safety, Integrity, Privacy, and other functional teams. Obtain decisions from the authorized owners for legal interpretation, external representations, and risk acceptance.
Improve operational workflows for content and privacy compliance while keeping implementation and operation of controls with the appropriate functional owners.
Simplify and automate repeated administrative work, test the results, and verify that the improvement is adopted and produces accurate, reliable outputs.
Learn the GRC security-control environment and participate in the team’s on-call rotation, with scope and expectations explained during the hiring process.
Communicate clearly, surface uncertainty early, incorporate feedback, and develop the domain knowledge needed for the next priority.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have practical experience building and operating AI safety/security and content-moderation programs, and can explain your own decisions, contribution, and results.
Have used agentic tooling to automate and improve to scaled processes
Understand relevant technical concepts across model evaluation, training and release, safety controls, content moderation, and post-launch operations, and can explain where specialist input is needed.
Have a strong understanding of relevant AI safety, content, and privacy requirements, including the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, and experience translating them into operating processes and controls with domain experts and Legal.
Have led regulatory responses and external compliance audits, and can distinguish supported claims from evidence gaps.
Have delivered complex cross-functional programs, scoped practical first increments, and adapted priorities when constraints changed.
Have improved or automated an operational workflow and verified its accuracy, usefulness, and ongoing ownership.
Can maintain precise records, navigate technical/compliance documentation and contract language, follow through on commitments, and judge what to resolve directly or escalate.
Communicate clearly in writing and conversation with technical teams, Legal, leadership, and external stakeholders; explain evidence, uncertainty, recommendations, and tradeoffs.
Work constructively through disagreement, learn from feedback, and take responsibility for outcomes. Privacy program-management experience is a plus.

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. Coordinate multiple workstreams across People, Technology, Engineering, Product, Operations, and regional teams to deliver agreed outcomes.
Establish and maintain project governance, including status reporting, RAID logs, decision registers, steering forums, and escalation paths.
Apply Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid delivery methods based on the needs and complexity of each programme.
Identify delivery risks and dependencies early, drive mitigation actions, and escalate decisions that could affect timelines or outcomes.
Use GenAI tools to improve project planning, status reporting, meeting documentation, risk analysis, and workflow efficiency while applying appropriate confidentiality and review controls.
Identify opportunities to improve PMO processes, templates, reporting standards, and delivery practices across the People Team.

Qualifications

At least 5 years of experience working as a Project Manager, leading complex projects, transformation initiatives, or technology-enabled process improvements.
Experience leading cross-functional projects involving Human Resources (HR), employee experience, or workforce-related processes, including enterprise systems implementation or large-scale software rollouts.
Strong understanding of software implementation, testing, rollout, change management, and adoption.
Experienced work through unclear requirements, prioritise competing demands, and convert ambiguity into structured delivery plans.
Experience managing projects with stakeholders across different countries, cultures, and departments.
Hands-on experience building AI, automation, or workflow solutions for real business problems.
Experience using AI tools and emerging technologies to improve productivity and workflows.'
Combine strategic thinking with hands-on project execution.

Good to Have

Experience applying human oversight, data protection, and risk controls when implementing AI solutions.
Experience leading M&A integration projects.
Project management certification such as PMP, PRINCE2, or equivalent.

Life at Grab

We have your back with Term Life Insurance and comprehensive Medical Insurance.
With GrabFlex, create a benefits package that suits your needs and aspirations.
Celebrate moments that matter in life with loved ones through Parental and Birthday leave, and give back to your communities through Love-all-Serve-all (LASA) volunteering leave
We have a confidential Grabber Assistance Programme to guide and uplift you and your loved ones through life's challenges.

Description

Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

We are looking for a Senior Program Manager to own the Voice of the Customer (VoC) program for Amazon Leo — a greenfield build spanning both consumer (B2C) and enterprise (B2B) customer segments. This is a high-visibility, cross-functional role responsible for designing and operating the systems that transform customer feedback into actionable business intelligence, driving continuous improvement across the full customer journey from purchase through active service. This role is the architect of tools, systems, and customer connections — someone with a strong appetite for big data, technical depth to build and operate analytics infrastructure, and marketing acumen to translate customer signals into compelling narratives that drive action across the organization.

You will set the strategy, build the operational infrastructure, and run the day-to-day program, working across product, engineering, customer service, field service, marketing, legal, and data science to close the loop on customer feedback at scale.

Key job responsibilities

Own end-to-end VoC program design and operations across B2C and B2B segments, including survey strategy, feedback touchpoint mapping, and escalation frameworks
Partner with third-party vendors and internal engineering teams to integrate survey delivery across web, in-app, email, and field service channels
Define and maintain VoC metrics, including CSAT, NPS, and operational proxy metrics, and establish escalation thresholds that trigger cross-functional action
Build and operate real-time monitoring mechanisms, including flash reports, dashboards, and daily standup cadences, especially during high-intensity launch windows
Lead cross-functional triage for customer-reported issues, routing signals to the appropriate owning teams (product, network engineering, hardware, CS, field service) and tracking resolution
Design and operate business review cadences (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly) that connect customer feedback to leadership decision-making
Collaborate with legal, privacy, and security teams to ensure survey and data handling practices meet compliance requirements
Define go/no-go quality gates for new market launches using VoC-derived customer satisfaction and service reliability metrics
Build and maintain the VoC analytics infrastructure in partnership with BI engineers, ensuring data from multiple feedback channels feeds a single source of truth

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience working cross functionally across several teams

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of driving process improvements experience
Knowledge of general AI tools
Experience in survey design and datasets
Experience building and operating customer feedback or VoC programs at scale
Background in consumer electronics, connectivity services, or hardware-as-a-service products
Experience managing VoC programs across both consumer and enterprise customer segments
Familiarity with AWS data and analytics services (QuickSight, S3, etc.)
Experience in a launch or early commercial stage environment; comfort operating under ambiguity with high urgency
Track record of building programs from scratch without inherited infrastructure or playbooks

Obsidian Solutions Group (OSG) is seeking an Intelligence Analyst II to support The Bureau of Diplomatic Security (DS). The Bureau of Diplomatic Security (DS) is the security and law enforcement arm of the U.S. Department of State (the Department). DS is a world leader in international investigations, threat analysis, cyber security, counterterrorism, security technology, and protection of people, property, and information. Its primary mission is to provide a safe and secure environment for the conduct of U.S. foreign policy. The Office of Security Technology (ST) supports the DS mission through the application and use of appropriate technical security countermeasures.

The Countermeasures Program (CMP) and Security Technology Operations (STO) divisions are operational components within ST. CMP is primarily responsible for worldwide technical countermeasures policy for the Department. Countermeasures policies enforce the protection of sensitive and classified information. CMP also manages the overseas technical surveillance countermeasures (TSCM) program.

Requirements

Develop and action innovative methodologies to identify and resolve analytic problems for the government customer. Analytical products will be of quality for senior DoS leadership. Research (using classified and unclassified sources) and then create and publish analytic support documents.

The Northern California High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (NC HIDTA) and the Northern California Regional Intelligence Center (NCRIC) are seeking applicants for the position of Intelligence Analyst
. This position is located at the Federal Building at 450 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, CA. The hours of service are Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m. Personnel assigned to the position may work 4 days a week with 10-hour workdays. Personnel may be assigned to work at off-site locations within the NC HIDTA/NCRIC area of responsibility. To learn more about the program visit: www.ncric.ca.gov.

The ideal candidate
for this position will be a motivated professional who:
Possess a bachelor’s degree in International Studies, Information Technology, Statistics, Mathematics, Information Management, Criminal Justice, or a related field.
Takes initiative on projects.
Employs critical thinking.
Works well independently and in a team setting and coordinates well with others.
Has experience participating in information-sharing initiatives for law enforcement.
Knowledgeable in the development and processing of the intelligence cycle.
Has the ability to collect and evaluate criminal intelligence information to develop criteria to measure the reliability of such information.
Knowledgeable in tactics, techniques, procedures, and intent of criminal actors.
Is proficient in computer operations including GIS mapping, word processing, data management, statistical analysis and software applications and networks.
Independently motivated to pursue new tools, technologies, and training opportunities.
Interested in researching, compiling, and analyzing threat information.
Demonstrates experience translating technical information for non-technical audiences.
Can analyze multiple sources and feeds of cyber threats and incident information for relevance and sharing to partners.
Is proficient in software applications and networks.
Can provide tactful assistance to the public, law enforcement and private sector partners often under time-sensitive conditions as well as provide awareness-level presentations to law enforcement, private sector, and general public.
Applies privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties protections within the analytic process and to analytic products, such as application of the 28 CFR Part 23 regulation and the handling of personally identifiable information (PII).

It is highly desirable that applicants possess one (1) year of experience working in the crime analysis and/or intelligence fields and have completed or are willing to complete training in one of the programs listed below, or its equivalent:

California State University, Crime and Intelligence Analysis Certificate
International Association of Crime Analysts – Certified Law Enforcement Analyst (CLEA) Program
Federal Bureau of Investigations Center for Intelligence Training
US Department of Homeland Security, Intelligence Training Academy, Basic Intelligence and Threat Analysis Course (BITAC)
Drug Enforcement Administration - Federal Law Enforcement Analyst Training (FLEAT)
Drug Enforcement Administration - Basic Intelligence Research Specialist (BIRS) Training
Federal Law Enforcement Training Center's (FLETC) Intelligence Analyst Training Program
International Association of Law Enforcement Intelligence Analysts (IALEIA) – Foundations of Intelligence Analysis Training (FIAT)
SANS, GIAC certification or similar Information Security or Cybersecurity Basics Training
National Computer Forensics Institute, Basic Investigation of Computer and Electronic Crimes
Naval Postgraduate School & US DHS Center for Homeland Defense and Security
Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) Certification
International Association of Emergency Managers (IAEM) Associate or Certified Emergency Manager Certification
TEEX Infrastructure Protection Certificate
FEMA, Emergency Management Institute, NIMS/ICS Training
Other training certification that demonstrates qualifications that meet or exceed competencies identified in the Common Competencies for State, Local, and Tribal Intelligence Analysts: (Analyst Professional Development Road Map).

NOTE:
The eligible list created from this recruitment will be used to fill at-will positions (unclassified, extra help or limited positions). Individuals hired as extra-help or limited term are not guaranteed permanent status at the end of the assignment. Unclassified positions are not covered by Civil Service Rules.

Examples Of Duties
Intelligence Analysts are responsible for:

Maintaining awareness of threats and vulnerabilities with potential impact to local law enforcement and critical infrastructure partners.
Developing written products and presentations analyzing current and emerging threats to communicate timely, actionable, and relevant intelligence to public and private sector partners.
Providing case support to mitigate crimes and hazards in the NC HIDTA/NCRIC area of responsibility and thoroughly documenting tactics, techniques, and procedures involved.
Producing threat assessments, vulnerability assessments, strategic reports and tactical and operational analytical products.
Conducting link chart analysis, call record analysis, geospatial analysis, and data entry.
Providing case support relating to investigations of drug trafficking, major crimes, money laundering, gangs, violent crime, and serial crime events.
Providing support during emergency events, planned special events, training events, and training exercises.
Responding to cyber incidents, defending against cyber-attacks, and producing relevant, timely and actionable cyber intelligence.

Qualifications
Licensure/Certification:
Possession of or acquisition of a valid certification in Crime and Intelligence Analysis within 12 months of appointment.

Education and Experience:
Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to qualify is:
Education equivalent to a Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Quantitative Analysis, Information Management, Criminal Justice or a related field.
One year of experience involving crime data collection, statistical research and analysis, and working with criminal intelligence automated systems design and implementation.

Knowledge of:

Methods and techniques used in researching, compiling, sorting, evaluating, and analyzing statistical, theoretical and factual criminal and offender information.
Computer operations including, GIS mapping, word processing, data management, and statistical analysis.
Distinction between crime patterns, series, and trends.
Cyber incident prevention, cyber incident response capabilities and fusion center responsibilities.
Business English.

Skill/Ability to:

Synthesize a large volume of cyber, vulnerability, and criminal threat data.
Communicate effectively orally and in writing.
Compose written reports sharing information to diverse audiences.
Read and interpret maps and other geographic information systems.
Work with personal computers, perform data entry and basic programming.
Make oral presentations.
Ability and willingness to testify in court.

Must successfully complete a thorough law enforcement background investigation prior to appointment and obtain a National Security Clearance within the first eighteen (18) months of employment. Upon receipt of a National Security Clearance, the employee must retain a Visitor Access Request (VAR) with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) throughout employment.

Job Description

Tiered Approach

In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

In 2025, the National Council of Justice (CNJ) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) established a partnership aimed at promoting innovation in cybersecurity for the Brazilian Judiciary. Project BRA/25/025 develops and implements tools and strategies to strengthen cybersecurity, digital preservation and information integrity, expanding the protection of the Judiciary’s systems and users.

The initiative strengthens institutional security and promotes transparency, good governance and the efficiency of judicial processes, contributing to resource savings and to a more agile Justice system for the benefit of citizens and society.

To this end, the project governance is organized into the following fronts:

Four Cross-cutting Coordination Axes

General Coordination;
Integrated Monitoring and Control Unit;
Technical and Operational Management Unit;
Training and Communication Unit;

Four Workstreams, Focused On

Regulatory compliance;
Operational conformity;
Network governance;
Promotion of a cybersecurity culture;

As this is a home-based position, the candidate is expected to have adequate working conditions, including the infrastructure and equipment necessary for the full performance of the activities.

Duties And Responsibilities

Contribute to a proactive, forward-looking cyber defense posture for the Judiciary, anticipating threats based on the intelligence produced and shared.

Intelligence Production and Threat Analysis

Conduct advanced analyses of threat actors, their motivations, capabilities and TTPs (Tactics, Techniques and Procedures), applying analytical models such as the Diamond Model and the Cyber Kill Chain.
Transform raw data from technical, open and internal sources into actionable intelligence to support proactive defense and improve incident containment, observing operational security (OPSEC) best practices in collection activities.
Support vulnerability prioritization based on the actual likelihood of exploitation in the current threat landscape.
Monitor open sources, forums, deep and dark web channels, and national and international technical reports to identify campaigns, data leaks and threats targeting the public sector and the Judiciary.

Strengthening Proactive Detection

Support the analysis of incident-related artifacts, logs and relevant technical evidence to extract relevant IoCs and TTPs.

Identify long-term cyberattack trends to guide investments and changes in the defense architecture.
Propose improvements to technical controls based on the evolution of identified threats.
Support External Attack Surface Management (EASM) activities by identifying exposed assets, leaked credentials and indicators of organizational exposure.

Integration with Capacity Building and Innovation

Promote the use of CTI frameworks (e.g., MITRE ATT&CK, Diamond Model, Cyber Kill Chain), OPSEC best practices and security data analysis.

Continuity, Reporting and Simulations

Promote the reuse of intelligence products across Incident Response, Threat Hunting, Vulnerability Management and Security Operations teams

jobs.title: Regulatory Research Analyst
jobs.description:
About Dune Strategy

Dune Strategy is a management consulting firm based in Dubai. We advise international investors, family groups and sovereign-linked entities on the commercial decisions that define their position in the region: market entry, regional expansion, transactions, joint ventures. The firm works from a current reading of the market, including how family ownership dynamics, regulatory shifts and sovereign capital priorities actually influence outcomes.
We keep the portfolio small on purpose. Partners stay in the commercial conversations where decisions get shaped, and research reaches the people making the call rather than being filtered on the way up. Clients come to us when a decision needs a real understanding of local counterparties and operating conditions that cannot be managed from a distant head office.
The Regulatory Research Analyst sits at the front end of that work: reading the rules, tracking the path, and writing the note a partner actually uses.

What You Will Do
Research regulatory frameworks, licensing requirements and policy positions across the region, and keep the picture current as things change.
Map counterparties: who owns what, who decides, who can block, and where a family or state-linked interest sits in the structure.
Assemble briefing material for partner-led meetings, short enough to be read in the car and precise enough to rely on.
Track a regulatory path over weeks or months and flag the moment a decision point moves.
Write the underlying note: the position, the reasoning, and what is still open.
Check the numbers and the filings before anything goes to a client.

What We Are Looking For
Clarity of thought. You can get to the point of a document and say what it changes.
Writing that holds up under a partner's read and then a client's read.
A pragmatic streak: you work with the material available rather than waiting for a complete file.
Comfort with incomplete information, ambiguity and questions that do not have a clean answer yet.
Discipline with sources. You know where a fact came from and you can show it.
Enough judgement to know which finding matters to the commercial call and which is background.

Helpful Background
An interest in finance, economics or politics, whether from study, earlier work or self-directed reading.
Arabic, French or another language used with regional counterparties.
Exposure to a sector with heavy regulation: financial services, energy, healthcare, real estate or telecoms.
Prior research work in a consultancy, advisory firm, bank, law firm or public body.
Practice reading legal or regulatory text and pulling out the operative clause.

None of these are requirements. They are simply useful starting points, and we would rather read a clear note than a long list of credentials.

What We Offer
A permanent, full-time role on a hybrid arrangement in Dubai.
Direct exposure to partners and to the commercial conversations themselves, not a summary of them afterwards.
Work across several sectors and structures rather than one narrow desk.
A view of how sovereign capital, family ownership and regulation combine in practice on live decisions.
Clear standards and a small team where the work you produce is read and used.

What Success Looks Like

After a year, you can take a question from a partner and come back with a briefing that stands on its own: the position, the reasoning, the open risks. You spot the commercial call earlier than you did on day one, because you have watched enough decisions move to recognise the shape of one. Counterparties know your name and answer your calls. You are trusted to sit in on a conversation and write the note that comes out of it, and the partners have stopped checking your sources because they no longer need to.

Position Summary

TCW’s Sustainable Investment Team is composed of analysts that have fundamental asset class, sectoral, and thematic coverage, while the Quantitative SI Analyst handles data, analytics, and portfolio construction algorithm development. The team works closely with fundamental investment analysts, product specialists, client services, compliance, and marketing professionals. The quantitative SI Analyst primarily collaborates with the Sustainable Investment Analysts to amplify and systematize their work but may also have independent relationships with quantitative counterparts in different business lines (e.g., Quantitative Investment Research, Portfolio Analytics Group, Risk Management). The Quantitative Analyst also collaborates with Technology in order to oversee the sustainable investing data infrastructure and integration of analytics into various tools and platforms.

The Quantitative SI Analyst position is a core member of the Sustainable Investment team and reports to the Head of Sustainable Investments. The Analyst is responsible for identifying, selecting and overseeing the stack of data and tools that comprise the team’s data and analytics platform. The Analyst serves as the team’s primary interface with Technology and oversees the architecture and implementation of the data and analytics platform. The Analyst presents results of the team’s work in a clear and understandable manner to a wide range of internal and external stakeholders, while staying current on relevant sustainability research literature and market developments.

Essential Duties

Maintains and builds upon the sustainability data and analytics platform, and serve as a highly regarded domain expert
Manages monthly, quarterly, annual, and ad hoc fund reporting for sustainable vehicles, partnering with relevant stakeholders across the firm to ensure accurate and timely dissemination
Support execution and project management of innovative sustainable investing analytics for counterparts across asset classes
Develops visualization and quantitative analysis of data, presentations, and other materials for a diverse set of partners, clients and senior decision makers
Collaborates with Technology to oversee the integration of sustainable investing analytics and data points into portfolio analytics, engagement, and reporting platforms
Serves as the primary relationship manager with sustainability data vendors; on an as needed basis, identifies, tests and evaluates new sources of sustainable data and propose additions to the existing array of datasets and tools
Engages, as necessary, with partners across the Firm including Technology, Procurement, Legal, Risk and Compliance to ensure the development and operation of sustainable investing data and analytics stack

Required Qualifications

Undergraduate degree in Mathematics, Economics, Statistics, Quantitative Finance, Computer Science, Data Science, or a similarly quantitative field
Minimum of 3 years of work experience in applying quantitative methods to sustainability in an investment setting, such as equity or fixed-income trading, sell-side research, or risk management operation
Experience with one or more statistical programming languages (Python preferred) and visualization software (PowerBI or Tableau)
Experience with database architecture, querying languages (SQL), and data management
Familiarity with financial market data sources (Bloomberg, Morningstar, Factset, Compustat, etc.) and environmental, social and governance (ESG) data frameworks (MSCI, ISS, S&P, etc.)
Strong and efficient research capabilities, with ability to assess and analyze a wide range of financial and alternative data sources

Professional Skills Qualifications

Judgment and Flexibility: Thinks about issues and develops solutions that thoughtfully consider the broader context. Positively deals with a shifting demand for time, priorities, and the rapid change of environment
Organization: Strong organization and record retention practices; maintains audit-grade records
Ownership and Initiative: Takes ownership for and “rolls up sleeves” to meet objectives
Excellence: Demonstrates accuracy and thoroughness. Ensures quality and demonstrates a strong attention to detail and follow-through. Commits to implementing best practices and continuous improvement
Teamwork: Cooperates with management, colleagues, and third parties and operates with humility. Seeks and is open to giving and receiving suggestions to develop better solutions and to make the team stronger
Communications: Demonstrates strong written skills and presents analysis, suggestions, and other information clearly and concisely; presence and self-confidence to interface with the key constituents of the firm including management teams of companies, deal professionals, service providers and others
Relationships and Influence: Naturally connects and builds strong relationships with others, demonstrating strong emotional intelligence and an ability to communicate clearly and persuasively. This includes networking, influencing, collaborating – and a proven ability to build trust with clients and other organizational partners
Ability to drive a process forward through completion, and to effectively prioritize competing objectives and urgent deadlines
A pattern of excellence, both personally and professionally, demonstrated by the individual’s education, career track record, intellect, and professional reputation; self-awareness, maturity, irreproachable integrity

Desired Qualifications

Familiarity with geospatial analysis tools (Google Earth Engine, ArcGIS, QGIS)
Familiarity with LLMs and AI tools
Familiarity with data warehouses and data processing engines like Snowflake and Databricks

This role requires candidates to work from a TCW office a minimum of four days a week. Flexibility for remote work is offered on one day, depending on business needs.

Estimated Compensation

Base Salary:
For CA based position, the base salary range is $150k. This represents base salary only.

Other Compensation and Benefits:
In addition to base salary, employees are eligible for a discretionary bonus and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support you and your family, invest in your health and wellbeing, and help build long-term financial security. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, retirement benefits, and paid time off.

These benefits reflect our commitment to supporting the health, wellbeing, and long-term financial security of our employees and their families.

jobs.title: Business Intelligence Analyst II
jobs.description:
About The Team/Role

The Business Intelligence Analyst II
serves as a technical architect and automation lead within one or more of the domain areas within the Global Risk Operations organization. You will leverage enterprise-approved tools—Tableau, Python, SQL, and RPA—to modernize legacy workflows and drive operational scale. This role is the bridge between theoretical efficiency and the deployment of hardened, audit-ready automation.

You are a change agent dedicated to the continuous improvement of the department’s technical and automation capabilities. Your success will be determined by your ability to modernize the risk landscape through governed self-service. You will be evaluated on three primary pillars - operational scale, efficiency and impact, and integrity and compliance.

How You'll Make An Impact

SOLUTION ENGINEERING & AUTOMATION DELIVERY

Workflow Transformation: Identify manual bottlenecks and engineer automated, self-service replacements that adhere to enterprise technical standards.
Infrastructure Lead: Build and maintain the technical infrastructure required to automate complex financial risk workflows across assigned regions.
Scaling through AI: Proactively integrate AI-driven technologies to eliminate manual touchpoints, creating a self-scaling environment that grows without increasing headcount.
Change Agency: Serve as a departmental catalyst for technical evolution, applying strategic thinking and process re-engineering to transform manual workflows into scalable, automated solutions.

ADVANCED ANALYTICS & DATA STEWARDSHIP

Strategic Data Assets: Transform raw data into strategic assets, utilizing advanced analytics to provide stakeholders with predictive insights.
Self-Service Ecosystems: Develop and manage standardized reporting environments (Power BI/Tableau) that empower stakeholders with real-time data while maintaining a single source of truth.
Efficiency Engineering: Design and deploy technical solutions specifically intended to drive measurable cost savings and mitigate operational risks.
Insight Delivery: Perform deep-dive analysis of trends to identify and illustrate emerging issues, providing management with clear direction and data-backed explanations.

OPERATIONAL EXECUTION & TECHNICAL INTEGRITY

Performance Tracking: Implement processes and reporting to track work items, volume, and turnaround time, ensuring accurate capture of required operational data.
Reporting Administration: Oversee the lifecycle of departmental reporting, including KPIs, management dashboards, and both scheduled and ad-hoc requirements.
Sustainable Automation: Deliver innovative alternatives to manual processes by continuously educating the team on current applications and automated technology.

COMPLIANCE, GOVERNANCE & SOLUTION INTEGRITY

Financial Controls and Compliance: Maintain rigorous standards for data integrity, ensuring all automated reports and workflows are fully compliant with regulatory and internal audit standards.
Technical Integrity: Oversee report administration and version control to ensure the longevity and reliability of deployed solutions.
Risk Mitigation: Ensure all self-service tools are built with robust error handling and audit trails to prevent operational drift.

These statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed rather than give an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities.

Experience You'll Bring

Minimum Required Qualifications for Consideration

Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Computer Science, Data Analytics, Finance) OR an equivalent combination of education and relevant technical experience.
2-4 years in a Finance or Risk Operations environment.
Foundational understanding of SOX or similar regulatory frameworks.
Proven history of successfully converting manual processes into automated, scalable workflows.
Proficiency in complex joins and ETL processes.
Python: Intermediate proficiency, specifically utilizing Pandas and NumPy for data manipulation.
RPA: Hands-on experience with enterprise platforms like UiPath or Power Automate.
Must have intermediate or better SQL and Oracle database experience, working with large data sets.
Must successfully pass a background investigation.

Competencies

Analytical mind that can trouble-shoot, problem solve, and think logically through multifaceted issues and provide clear direction and explanation.
Ability to effectively and calmly operate within a complex, fast-paced and changing environment.
Self-motivated, solution oriented and results driven.
Effective verbal and written communication skills
Excellent time management, prioritization skills, goals setting, planning and work scheduling skills.
Superior critical thinking and problem solving skills
Strong attention to detail with the ability to recognize and react to discrepancies.
Emerging Tech: Experience with Prompt Engineering and building RAG systems or using LLM APIs to enhance automation.
SAS programming skills.
Experience interpreting contractual terms.
Knowledge of WEX systems and business processes.
A high degree of professional curiosity and a "systems thinking" approach to problem-solving.

jobs.title: Network Loss Program Manager, Amazon Transportation Brazil
jobs.description:
Description

Are you looking for the opportunity to create substantial impact on business profitability through the reduction of operational waste across one of Amazon's fastest-growing markets? The Network Losses Program Manager role in Brazil is that opportunity.

As a Network Loss Program Manager, you will own the end-to-end strategy and execution of network loss reduction across Brazil's Fulfillment Center (FC) and Transportation networks. You will be responsible for overseeing network loss metrics, driving operational improvements, and managing product implementations that eliminate shrinkage, damages, concessions, and undeliverable losses across the entire supply chain. The scope of impact spans Transportation Losses, FC Losses (Warehouse Lost, Warehouse Damage, FC Shrinkage, Item Missing), and seller reimbursement optimization — working in close collaboration with FC/Transportation Operations, ACES, SL&P, NCRC, Products, Finance, and RoW Network Losses teams.

At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. Our team drives innovation while supporting continuous operational improvement. Brazil's network loss landscape presents a unique challenge: with several initiatives across three workstreams, a rapidly expanding warehouse footprint, and a complex reverse logistics network, this role requires someone who can connect the dots across multiple programs, drive accountability through mechanisms, and deliver measurable financial impact.

This opportunity requires excellent troubleshooting, problem solving, and the ability to succeed in a fast-paced, ambiguous, and technical environment. Ownership of work is extremely important, and candidates should have a proven record of driving operations, process fixes, and strategic initiatives to completion. The ideal candidate is motivated, data-driven, and agile — with strong cross-functional influencing skills and the ability to operate at both strategic and tactical levels.

Key job responsibilities

Metrics Ownership: Own and manage Brazil's Network Loss metrics including Transportation Shrinkage, Warehouse Losses, Reimbursements and DPMO across In-Facility, In-Transit, and On-Road segments. Monitor success metrics on a daily/weekly basis through WBRs and MBRs. Deep dive operational data to identify root causes for losses across the network.
Product & Process Implementation: Drive product implementation in operations (e.g., URL compliance, TEP expansion, recovery mechanisms, repacking programs, reverse network design) and operational process solutions to eliminate losses. Partner with RoW Products to adapt global solutions to Brazil's context. Manage and expand loss recovery programs including 3P carrier. Track financial impact and drive accountability.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with FC Operations, Transportation, Continuous Improvement, Quality, Loss Prevention, Finance to build visibility on loss themes, set up mitigation plans.
Reverse Logistics & ReLo Center: Support the design and operationalization of Brazil's Reverse Logistics (ReLo) Center, driving improvements in undeliverable grading, sellable yield, and recommerce recovery rates.
Standardization & Governance: Improve operational processes by standardizing metrics, SOPs, and governance mechanisms across Brazil's FC and transportation network.
Stakeholder Communication: Communicate results, risks, and strategic recommendations to senior leadership through structured mechanisms including WBRs, MBRs, and STL syncs.

Basic Qualifications

Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience in program or project management
Experience in supply chain

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
Experience leading process improvements

jobs.title: Business Analyst I, Ops Tech Solutions Delivery
jobs.description:
Description

Join the Global Workforce Management (GWM) team as a Business Analyst where you will shape how Amazon plans and optimizes workforce operations across global field teams.

The Global Workforce Management team develops and maintains a unified, data-driven approach to predict demand volume and staffing scenarios. As a Business Analyst in this role, you will implement workforce planning processes that complement Service Desk forecasting, create comprehensive documentation and training materials, and support strategic workforce planning initiatives that enable better operational decisions across global regions.

In this position, you will collaborate with the Workforce Planning Lead and cross-functional teams to translate complex operational requirements into clear, actionable processes. Your work will include documenting methodologies, gathering stakeholder requirements, preparing business reviews, and identifying opportunities for process improvements that enhance workforce planning effectiveness.

Key job responsibilities

Implement workforce planning processes that integrate with Service Desk forecasting and field operations requirements
Create and maintain process documentation, including workflows, standard operating procedures, training materials, and workforce planning playbooks
Gather requirements from cross-functional stakeholders and support communications regarding workforce planning initiatives
Prepare business reviews, presentations, and communication materials for leadership and operational teams
Analyze workforce planning data to identify process gaps, inefficiencies, and improvement opportunities
Support the measurement and tracking of workforce planning metrics and initiative impacts
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive adoption and compliance of standardized workforce planning processes

A day in the life

As a Business Analyst on the GWM team, you will work closely with the Workforce Planning Lead, Service Desk teams, and field operations leaders across global regions. Your day will involve analyzing operational data to understand workforce planning requirements, documenting processes with clear steps and success criteria, and creating materials that help stakeholders understand and adopt new methodologies.

You will participate in cross-functional meetings to gather requirements and ensure workforce planning processes meet business needs. You will solve defined workforce planning challenges, identify risks to process implementation, and escalate complex issues to senior team members when appropriate. Your work directly supports strategic planning decisions that affect how Amazon staffs and manages field operations globally.

Internal stakeholders include workforce planning teams, operations managers, Service Desk forecasting teams, and regional field operations leaders. You will help these teams understand how standardized processes improve planning accuracy and operational efficiency.

About The Team

The Global Workforce Management team is dedicated to building data-driven workforce planning capabilities that support Operations Technology Solutions and expanding organizations. The team operates across global regions, bringing together expertise in forecasting, capacity planning, and operational analytics.

The team values collaboration, continuous improvement, and data-driven decision making. Team members work together to develop methodologies and tools that enable better workforce planning across Amazon's diverse operational landscape. The team culture emphasizes clear communication, attention to detail, and a commitment to delivering sustainable solutions that scale across the organization.

Basic Qualifications

1+ years of complex Excel VBA macros writing experience
Bachelor's degree or equivalent
Experience defining requirements and using data and metrics to draw business insights
1+ years of business analyst, data analyst or similar role experience
Experience in data analysis using tools such as Excel, Pivot Tables, SQL, Tableau, or equivalent

Preferred Qualifications

Experience using very large datasets
Experience in capacity planning, operations planning, business analysis or equivalent
Experience in process improvement
Experience with data visualization using Tableau, Quicksight, or similar tools
Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience in technical support

jobs.description:
Transdev’s TAS division is at the forefront of autonomous mobility operations, partnering with leading AV technology companies to deploy, operate, and scale driverless transportation services.

We are seeking a high-impact Six Sigma Black Belt to lead operational excellence across autonomous vehicle (AV) driving and servicing environments. This role is responsible for designing, optimizing, and scaling processes that ensure safety, efficiency, and reliability in AV fleet operations.

You will work at the intersection of operations, technology, and field execution, driving measurable improvements in a rapidly evolving, high-visibility business.

Overview

We expect all team members to champion Company standards of conduct and our inclusive culture. Transdev provides a broad range of services for our clients autonomous driving testing and service development efforts.

In this role, you will serve as a key member of the Forecasting, Planning, and Strategy team, supporting Transdev Alternative Services’ autonomous mobility initiatives. You will be responsible for developing financial models, business cases, and market analyses to support large-scale AV deployments. This role combines strategic analysis, financial planning, and cross-functional coordination to support investment decisions, operational planning, and long-term business growth in a rapidly evolving industry.

Transdev Is Proud To Offer

Competitive compensation package of minimum $177,195.20 – maximum $185,161.60

Benefits Include

Vacation: minimum of two (2) weeks
Sick days: 5 days
Holidays: 12 days; 8 standard and 4 floating
Other standard benefits: 401(k) retirement plan, medical, dental and vision, life insurance, short-term disability, voluntary long-term disability.

Benefits may vary depending on location policy. The above represents the standard Corporate Policy.

Key Responsibilities

Support labor planning activities and forecasting for USA and international AV operations.
Perform data analysis and data tool development for TAS partnering with the Data team.
Identify and evaluate strategic business opportunities for autonomous vehicle services through market analysis, financial modeling, and ecosystem assessment.
Lead the development of financial models, including P&L projections, cost structures, CAPEX estimates, and operational assumptions to support large-scale AV deployments and investment decisions.
Prepare detailed business cases and scenario analyses (e.g., pricing, utilization, scalability) to support executive decision-making and long-term strategy.
Conduct market research, competitive benchmarking, and technology analysis to identify trends, risks, and growth opportunities within the autonomous mobility ecosystem.
Develop marketing materials to highlight Transdev’s autonomous mobility capabilities and support commercial outreach.
Support RFQ and proposal development by providing analytical inputs, including financial projections, cost modeling, and operational feasibility assessments.
Coordinate partnership discussions with technology providers, mobility operators, and investors involved in autonomous mobility programs.
Develop internal tools, models, and frameworks to standardize financial analysis, forecasting, and business case development across projects.
Contribute to continuous improvement of internal processes, financial planning methodologies, and strategic frameworks.

to help transform complex healthcare data into meaningful insights that improve quality, reduce costs, and support better healthcare decision-making.
